## Function Validate Record

Turns a parsed record document into a typed Contour Record, or every problem it has.

Behaviour: validateRecord(doc: unknown). A doc that is not a plain object (null, an array, a scalar) → {ok: false, problems: ["(root): a record must be an object"]}. Otherwise every object is checked against its key table, the whole Contour key set plus V2's extensions (P34, issue #44; contour.schema.json of the Contour author): root: version, System, Actor, Requirement, Guardrail; System: name, description, requirements, guardrails, groups, dependencies; Component: name, description, language, requirements, guardrails, uses, functions, dataObjects, interfaces, events, references, consumes, dependsOn; Function: name, description, behavior, requirements, guardrails, preconditions, steps, examples; example: given, when, then, ref; Data Object: name, description, schema, requirements, guardrails; Event: name, description, requirements, guardrails, schema; Interface: name, description, exposes, requirements, guardrails, schema; Actor: name, description, uses, requirements, guardrails; Requirement and Guardrail: name, description; a dependency: name, version, language, doc. Per object, in this order: each required key that is missing ("<path>.<key>: required" — a problem), each key not in the table in the object's own order ("<path>: unknown key '<k>' (ignored)" — a WARNING, never a problem; its value is not read), then the present keys' values in the table's order, depth first. Required: the root's System; every name and description (Event included); System.groups; an example's given, when, then; an Interface's exposes. A Function's behavior and examples are NOT required (absent: behavior "", examples []). version, when present, must be 1 ("version: must be 1"); absent means 1. Texts must be non-empty strings and are stored trimmed; lists must be lists; list items that are elements must be objects; examples and exposes, when present, must not be empty; a step is an object with exactly one key, a verb of calls, reads, modifies, produces, uses, whose value is a non-empty string. requirements, guardrails, references, consumes, dependsOn, exposes and an Actor's uses are lists of non-empty strings (stored trimmed). Actor is one object (→ one Actor, path "Actor") or a list (paths "Actor[i]"); anything else → "Actor: must be an object or a list". A schema (Data Object, Event, Interface) is a non-empty string (trimmed), or a mapping: a mapping whose every value is a string keeps today's text, each value trimmed and non-empty ("<path>.schema.<k>: must be a non-empty string"), stored as JSON.stringify(mapping, null, 2) in the document's key order; a mapping holding any other value (a mapping, a list, a number, a boolean, null) is stored as JSON.stringify of it with the keys of every mapping at every depth sorted ascending, indent 2 (the old reader's json.dumps sort_keys); anything else → "<path>.schema: must be a non-empty string". A Component name repeated in the record, a Function name repeated in its Component, a Data Object name repeated anywhere in the record and an Event name repeated anywhere in the record is a problem at the repeat's name ("duplicate Component|Function|Data Object|Event name '<n>'"). Absent lists become [], absent language, ref and schema become null. Dependencies (P19): System.dependencies is a list of objects, each requiring name, version and language (texts, trimmed; doc an optional text, null when absent); a name repeated → "<path>.name: duplicate dependency name '<n>'"; a version (trimmed) not matching /^v?[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)*([-+][0-9A-Za-z.+-]+)?$/ → "<path>.version: must be an exact version (got '<v>')" (no range, tag or wildcard). Component.uses is a list; per item in order: not a non-empty string → "<path>[i]: must be a non-empty string"; its trimmed text not among the declared names → "<path>[i]: unknown dependency '<n>' (declared: <names joined by ', ', or none>)"; a name already listed before it → "<path>[i]: dependency '<n>' repeated". The declared names are read from the document before the groups are walked: the trimmed name of every item of System.dependencies that is an object with a non-empty string name, distinct, in order. Absent dependencies and uses become []. Whether a dependency's language fits the Component is the planner's check (the Component's language may come from the map). Any problem → {ok: false, problems} (all of them, document order; the warnings are dropped); none → {ok: true, record}, plus a third key warnings (document order) only when there is at least one. The paths read System.groups[0].functions[3].examples[0].then; the root is "(root)".

Steps:
- reads: Contour Record
- produces: Record Result

## Component requirements / guardrails

Requirements:
- Strict TypeScript: tsconfig strict, ESM, no `any`; every module compiles with tsc --noEmit.
- One Document Out: Every command prints exactly one JSON document on stdout and nothing else; the human log goes to stderr.
- Deterministic Core: cards and compiler give byte-identical results for the same inputs: no clock, no randomness, no environment reads. acceptance is bound only in its pure parts (Snapshot Targets, Build Attempt Diff): Run Acceptance spawns a shell and its only timer is the child's timeout; env and the timeout are parameters, never process.env (06.10, P3). processor reads the environment only in Read Registry; Assemble Request, Read Response, Stub Answer, Assemble Batch and Read Batch are pure of clock and network; the transport and its sleep are parameters of Send Generation and Send Batch (P4, P11). git spawns only in Run Git, synchronously, with the child's environment given whole as a parameter; it reads no process.env and no clock of its own (P6). cli touches the process only in its entry src/cli.ts: the environment, the working directory, the clock and the output streams reach main() as parameters, and the environment reaches the processor only through Read Registry (P7). language is pure data and pure functions: no clock, no environment, no file system, no child process; node:path is its only Node module; its shell lines are text (P8). contour reads no file, no clock and no environment: it parses the text it is given; the package yaml is imported in Parse Document alone (P9). planner reads no file, no clock and no environment: the cli reads the record and the map and passes which files exist as a function; node:path is its only Node module (P10a). builder reads no file, no clock and no environment: the caller passes the checks, the cards, the profile and the texts of the guard, the locator and the probes; node:path is its only Node module (P10b). primer reads files and spawns git (git's gitOk, the environment a parameter) only in Primer Command, the clock only there through deps.now; Read Runs, Read Story and Render Primer are pure functions of what they are given, no network anywhere (P12a). scout reads no clock, no environment and no network and spawns nothing: Parse Turn, Spend Budget and Seed From Ownership are pure; Cage Path and Run Tool reach the file system only through the ScoutFs parameter (realpath, readFile); elapsed time is a parameter; node:path is its only Node module (P13a). scout-session reaches the model only through the processor's Send Generation and the clock only through deps.now; Run Scout reads the tree through the ScoutFs parameter; Scout Command and Plan From Scout are the scout layer's two node:fs files (git through gitOk and runGit, node:crypto for the sha256 in Scout Command), the environment a parameter (P13b). reviewer's checks (Find Obligations, Check Envelope, Check Guardrails, Plan Mutants, Render Findings) are pure functions of the record, git's outputs and the texts they are given: no file, no clock, no environment, no child process, no Node module (P14a). review-session spawns only through acceptance's Run Acceptance (the mutant runs, each under its timeout) and git's Run Git; Run Mutants writes only through acceptance's Restore Snapshot; Review Command is the reviewer layer's one node:fs file (the record, the map and scout.json read, the review written), the environment a parameter, no clock and no model call (P14b). debt spawns only through acceptance's Run Acceptance and git's Run Git, reads the deck file, the card's files and the run archive through node:fs, no clock and no model call; the environment is a parameter (P17). scaffold reads the template folders and writes the new project through node:fs (node:url only to find the package root from its own module file), spawns nothing, reads no clock and no environment (P18).
- Node Only: Runtime dependencies: Node 20 built-ins and the package `yaml` (the record reader), nothing else; dev dependencies pinned exactly, no ^ or ~.

Guardrails:
- No Network In Tests: tests/setup.ts makes fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket and net.connect throw "network blocked in tests"; only the processor's own transport is mocked.
- No Shell Outside Acceptance: child processes are spawned only by Run Acceptance, the git module (in Run Git alone, P6) and the processor's none; everything else is pure.
- Frozen Tree During Run: while a run is in flight no file outside the cards' targets and .morph/ changes; a changed declared input discards the answer unread.

Write the files: `src/contour/types.ts`, `src/contour/record.ts`.

## Function Layer Edges

For every code directory of the record, the directories it may import.

Behaviour: layerEdges(record, map) → Layer Edges Result, over the WHOLE record and map (never a cut's subset). Per Component C in record order: profile = Resolve Profile(C.language, map.language), an error → "Component '<C>': <it>". Per Function F of C: its unit is the first map group whose functions hold F's name, else F; the unit name is that group's name, else F's name; targets = the targets of the map card whose id is slugName(unit name) when that card gives targets, else [code, test] of Name Targets(profile, C.name, unit name) (an error → "Component '<C>': <it>"); dirs(F) = path.posix.dirname of each of codeTargets(profile, targets) (test files and other extensions left out; "." for a root file), distinct. C's directories = the union of dirs(F) over its Functions. Every directory of every dirs(F) is a key of edges. Per step `uses: X` of a Function F (of any Component): X names a Component when X equals its name or componentSlug(X) equals componentSlug(its name); X is a dependency when a System dependency is named exactly X. Both → the error "Function '<F>': 'uses: <X>' names the Component '<that Component's name>' and the dependency '<X>'". A Component only → for each d of dirs(F), every directory of that Component but d itself joins edges[d]. A dependency or neither → nothing (a module: Component.uses and the guard's module argument). Then, after C's Functions, per name X of C.dependsOn (Contour's own Component → Component edge, P34, issue #44), in order: X names a Component (its name equals X or componentSlug equals componentSlug(X)) → for each directory d of C, every directory of that Component but d itself joins edges[d]; no Component → the error "Component '<C>': dependsOn '<X>' names no Component of the record". Any error → {ok: false, errors} (record order, each text once); else {ok: true, edges}: the keys and each list sorted ascending by code unit, no duplicates; a directory whose Functions use no Component maps to [].

Steps:
- reads: Contour Record
- reads: Contour Map
- uses: contour
- uses: language
- produces: Layer Edges Result

## Function Card Layers

The part of the edges one card's guard gets — its code directories.

Behaviour: cardLayers(profile, targets, edges) → an object: for each directory d of codeTargets(profile, targets) (path.posix.dirname, "." for a root file; distinct, first seen first, so the keys keep that order) the entry d → edges[d] when edges has the own key d, else []. No code target → {}.

- reads: Layer Edges Result
- produces: Record<string, string[]>

## Function Layers Arg

The guard's layers argument, after the module argument of builder's allowArg.

Behaviour: layersArg(allowed, layers) → string. layers undefined → "" (the guard line stays byte for byte). Else the module argument's placeholder " ''" when allowed is empty (allowArg wrote nothing there), then " '" + JSON.stringify(layers) + "'". The guards of contract 2 (templates/go and templates/typescript decks/tools/guard.mjs, the line "// morph-guard-contract: 2") read it as the fourth argument of `src`: given, the "layers" key of layers.json is not read; Go keys a package by its directory, TypeScript a file by its first folder under src/ (the argument's directories mapped the same way); an import of another key not in the importing key's list is red: Go "guard: package <dir> imports <import path>: the record has no 'uses' from <dir> to <target dir> (allowed: <list joined by ', '> or none)", TypeScript "guard: <file>:<line> layer <layer> imports layer <layer2>: the record has no 'uses' from <layer> to <layer2> (allowed: … or none)".
